newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-WHITAKER/DE LA HOYA POUND-FOR-POUND SHOWDOWN APRIL 12.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-WHITAKER/DE LA HOYA POUND-FOR-POUND SHOWDOWN APRIL 12.

text.p: Pernell Whitaker may have lost a step, but the welterweight champion says he is not about to lose his unofficial status as the world's best pound-for-pound fighter when he meets young Oscar de la Hoya on April 12.

"The kid is a good fighter, but Pernell Whitaker is the master," the 33-year-old American said Tuesday at a news conference to promote the Las Vegas bout. "Oscar de la Hoya may be the Boy Wonder, but I'm Batman."

In a refreshing contrast to the usual business of boxing where big names put off showdown matches to milk as much money as they can from safe opponents, Whitaker and de la Hoya, 23, are giving the public what it wants -- a glamour bout between two of boxing's best respected fighters.

Billed as "Pound for Pound - Libra Por Libra", Whitaker, 40-1-1, is putting his World Boxing Council welterweight title on the line against WBC super lightweight champion de la Hoya, 23-0, in a new outdoor stadium at Caesars Palace.
Said de la Hoya, "We need big, super fights in boxing. April 12 will be an historic night. It is going to be electrifying. You're not going to see anything like this for another 10 years.
"Boxing needs it. It's like healing up a bruise on boxing."
De la Hoya, who has stopped all but three of his professional opponents within the distance, will earn a guaranteed $10 million. Whitaker is guaranteed $6 million.

De la Hoya expressed great respect for Whitaker, but said the veteran's struggle in Atlantic City last Friday against Cuban-born Diobelis Hurtado revealed the inevitable wear and tear of a long career.
"Once you're a professional fighter for 10 years, you're not the same," said the handsome de la Hoya, boxing's Golden Boy since winning the lone U.S. Olympic title in 1992.
"You take a lot of punishment. Pernell Whitaker will try to be in the best shape but his footwork is not there, not like before."
Las Vegas oddsmakers have made de la Hoya a 3-1 favourite.

Whitaker, whose fast feet, flashing hands and dazzling defence have long frustrated opponents, almost blew his big payday as he barely beat Hurtado. Knocked down twice by Hurtado, Whitaker needed an 11th-round knockout to keep the date with de la Hoya.

"I'm still quick," said Whitaker about his footwork that used to make him boast he could "disappear" in the ring. "If it's a little slower I'll just have to use something else, but I don't feel like I've lost a step at all.
"I think this one will be for the history books."

De la Hoya does not plan to test how effective he can be 10 years from now. His goal is to arrange numerous big paydays in the next three or four years and then get out of boxing with his wealth, health and dark good lucks all intact.

De la Hoya, whose game plan is to go to college and study architecture, said: "I'm going to be faster than him and I'll have the power to try and knock him out. At 147 (pounds, 67 kg) I'm going to be very strong."

His pretty boy countenance and fighting style kept him at first from winning approval from the Mexican community back home in Los Angeles. But victories over a string of top-notch Mexican and Mexican-American fighters brought to de la Hoya a grudging respect from his community.
"I haven't got cut, I haven't got hurt," said de la Hoya.
"The Mexican style is you've got to be tough. I want to be a smart boxer. I'm not looking to get cut, bruised, have a broken nose. I'm willing to exchange with anybody but in a smart way."
Whitaker said de la Hoya's more orthodox boxing style should suit him better than the awkward attacks launched by Hurtado that kept the champion off balance in Atlantic City.
"I will be at my best and that will be better than his best," he said.
Asked if he thought he needed to beat de la Hoya to cement his place in boxing history, Whitaker, whose only loss came by decision against Jose Ramirez in 1988, looked offended.
"You can bronze me now," he said, justifiably proud of his ring record.
